methods.name: createDashboard
methods.title: Create Dashboard
methods.description: Each inline query is validated by the same translation the query surface performs, against the caller's view of the catalog. id, owner_id, owner_email, generation, the timestamps and permissions are server-assigned and rejected if supplied. A public dashboard requires SAVED_QUERY_PUBLISH.

methods.name: createOtelSink
methods.title: Create Otel Sink
methods.description: Creates one catalog source table per opted-in signal and materializes it in ClickHouse, then records the sink. All-or-nothing: if any signal's table cannot be created the tables created so far are dropped and no sink is recorded. Rejected if the sink name is taken (409), a derived table name is taken (409), or the name or signal set is invalid (422 — every rule about this body is reported that way, never as a binding 400). The returned `endpoint` is what an OTLP/HTTP exporter should be pointed at — it appends /v1/logs, /v1/traces or /v1/metrics itself.

methods.name: createPipeline
methods.title: Create Pipeline
methods.description: Stores a pipeline. Only `name`, `kind` and `target` are required: every other declaration member may be authored later by PATCH while the pipeline is disabled. The gate its `kind` selects runs when the pipeline is armed — by this call for an `enrich` pipeline registered with `enabled: true`, else by the PATCH that enables it — and on preview of a disabled pipeline. An `aggregate` pipeline always lands disabled: preview it, then enable it via PATCH. A field belonging to the other kind is rejected with 422 rather than ignored.

responses.description: The calling identity may not read a column the declaration reads: one a column policy hides from it (`column_not_entitled`, checked first), or a `sensitive` one it lacks the clearance for (`sensitive_column_not_entitled`); or it lacks the endpoint's privilege or the pipeline's grant

methods.name: createSavedQuery
methods.title: Create Saved Query
methods.description: The body is validated by the same translation the matching translate-only endpoint performs, so a saved query is always executable as stored. id, owner_id, source, generation and the timestamps are server-assigned and rejected if supplied.

methods.name: createTable
methods.title: Create Table
methods.description: Records the table identity as PENDING and issues no ClickHouse DDL. Define its physical schema and materialize it via POST /{name}/schema. Columns and physical keys are not accepted here (422).

methods.name: defineTableSchema
methods.title: Define Table Schema
methods.summary: Define and materialize a table's schema
methods.description: Sets the complete physical schema (columns plus physical keys — ordering_key/partition_by for a source, grain_key/cardinality for an enrichment — and an optional row-expiry ttl) of a not-yet-materialized table and issues CREATE TABLE in ClickHouse, flipping it to ACTIVE. Rejected if already materialized (409) or the schema is incomplete/inconsistent (422); on a ClickHouse failure the table is marked FAILED and may be retried. For an **enrichment**, the five provenance columns are **injected** if you do not declare them — `pipeline_generation` (long), `model` (string), `enriched_at` (timestamp), `group_version` (long), `truncated` (boolean) — appended in that order with the `system` tag. A provenance column you declare yourself is left exactly as you declared it: injection only ever adds, never duplicates, overwrites or reorders. `model`, `group_version` and `truncated` stay empty on an enrichment computed by a `sql` transform, which makes no model call and has no group. The retired `evaluator_version` is not injected: nothing has written it since the evaluator was folded into its pipeline. Re-defining a PENDING or FAILED table without a column a column policy lists prunes it from that list; one that would empty a list is refused 409 `column_in_column_policy` before any CREATE. 409 `table_busy` when another change to the table holds it past the lock timeout (retry).

methods.name: deleteOtelSink
methods.title: Delete Otel Sink
methods.description: Drops every catalog table backing the sink's signals (ClickHouse table and catalog rows) and removes the sink. A signal whose table is already gone is skipped.

methods.name: deletePipeline
methods.title: Delete Pipeline
methods.description: Removes the process. The target table and its rows are left intact — a target that stops being fed is stale, not invalid.

methods.name: deleteTable
methods.title: Delete Table
methods.description: Drops the ClickHouse table. Blocked (409) if a source still has enrichments, or if a pipeline reads this table as its input — that dependency breaks here rather than at the pipeline's next refresh. A pipeline whose *target* this is goes with the table instead: it exists only to fill it. Deleting an enrichment prunes its `<enrichment>.<column>` names from its source's column policies (bumping the source's access generation), and is refused 409 `column_in_column_policy` when a list would empty. 409 `table_busy` when another change to the table holds it past the lock timeout (retry).

methods.name: deleteTableAccess
methods.title: Delete Table Access
methods.description: Removes the role's entry (privileges, rows and columns) and increments the table's access generation. `generation` is optional: without it the entry is removed whatever changed since it was read; with it, a value above the table's generation or older than the role's last change is refused 409 access_conflict, and a non-integer one 422. Checks run in this order: 400 for a missing, blank or repeated role, 403 without TABLE_GRANT, 404 for an unknown table, 422 unusable generation, 404 when the role has no entry, 409 access_conflict. 409 table_busy when another change to the table holds it past the lock timeout.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Raw provider role, sent as an ordinary URL-encoded query value (role `/analytics/viewers` is `?role=%2Fanalytics%2Fviewers`, `team%ops` is `?role=team%25ops`). Any character is allowed. Trimmed; blank, or given more than once, is 400 bad_request. Missing is 400 bad_request too.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: Optional: the table's access generation as last read, an integer

responses.description: access_conflict (the role changed since it was read) or table_busy

methods.name: executeQuery
methods.title: Execute Query
methods.description: Translates the structured query to ClickHouse SQL and runs it against the entity named in `entity`. Returns the projected rows and, for row-mode offset paging with `include_total`, the total match count. Unknown entities, fields, functions, or unsupported features are rejected with HTTP 400.

responses.description: Unknown entity/field/function or unsupported query feature
Query exceeded the configured execution budget (`query_budget_exceeded`): the wall-clock or memory ceiling in `query.budget.*`. Deterministic — narrow the query rather than retrying.

methods.name: executeQueryCsv
methods.title: Execute Query Csv
methods.summary: Execute a structured query, returning CSV
methods.description: Runs the structured query exactly as `/v1/queries/execute` does — same request body, validation, default limit 100 and maximum limit 1000 (a higher limit is rejected, never clamped), budget and errors — and returns the result as an RFC 4180 CSV attachment: UTF-8 without a BOM, CRLF line ends, a header row that is present even when no row matches. A null cell is an empty field, the empty string is `""`, arrays and objects are compact JSON text, and nothing is escaped for spreadsheets. `totalCount` (offset paging with `include_total`) is returned in the `X-Total-Count` header. Errors are `ErrorView` JSON.

headers.name: X-Total-Count
headers.description: Total matching rows; only for row-mode offset paging with include_total=true

responses.description: Unknown entity/field/function or unsupported query feature
Query exceeded the configured execution budget (`query_budget_exceeded`).

methods.name: executeSql
methods.title: Execute Sql
methods.description:
Translates a single read-only SQL SELECT statement to the structured query DSL and runs it through the same pipeline as `/v1/queries/execute`, with the same governance: entity and field validation, the closed function catalog, default limit 100, and maximum limit 1000 on the outermost statement (a higher LIMIT is rejected, never clamped). Accepted: joins (INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL/CROSS, with at least one equality in ON), non-recursive CTEs, derived tables of any accepted shape, uncorrelated IN/EXISTS/scalar subqueries, CASE, arithmetic operators and window functions (row_number/rank/dense_rank and count/sum/avg/min/max OVER), and set operations. Set operations follow ClickHouse rather than the SQL standard, so the same text means the same thing here and against the database: a bare INTERSECT or EXCEPT means ALL, a bare UNION is rejected (ClickHouse has no default union mode), MINUS is rejected (ClickHouse has no such keyword), and a trailing ORDER BY/LIMIT applies to the LAST BRANCH — wrap the operation (`SELECT * FROM (<set operation>) ORDER BY ...`) to order or limit the combined result. Rejected before execution: WITH RECURSIVE, correlated subqueries, general CAST, ROLLUP/CUBE and functions outside the catalog. Outer joins yield NULL for an unmatched side. `LIKE` and `ILIKE` are supported only for `'%text%'` patterns, each with standard semantics: `LIKE` matches case-sensitively, `ILIKE` case-insensitively. Returns the projected rows; `totalCount` is never populated (the key is omitted).

A statement whose tables are all in `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` (`TABLES`, `COLUMNS`, `SCHEMATA`) is answered from ADAS's own catalog instead, in the same response envelope. Because it never reaches ClickHouse, none of the governance above applies to it: no default limit, no maximum limit, and a wider expression surface (arithmetic and CAST included) — its size is bounded by the catalog. It cannot be combined with a queryable entity, and a construct the in-process evaluator cannot answer correctly (a join, a subquery, a window function, a DISTINCT aggregate) is rejected with 400.

responses.description: SQL parse/validation failure or unsupported SQL construct
Query exceeded the configured execution budget (`query_budget_exceeded`): the wall-clock or memory ceiling in `query.budget.*`. Deterministic — narrow the query rather than retrying.

methods.name: executeSqlCsv
methods.title: Execute Sql Csv
methods.summary: Execute an ad-hoc SQL SELECT, returning CSV
methods.description: Runs the statement exactly as `/v1/queries/execute-sql` does — same SQL subset, governance, limits, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` handling and errors — and returns the result as an RFC 4180 CSV attachment in the format `/v1/queries/execute-csv` describes. The header row carries the same column names execute-sql uses as row keys.

responses.description: SQL parse/validation failure or unsupported SQL construct
Query exceeded the configured execution budget (`query_budget_exceeded`).

methods.name: exportCatalog
methods.title: Export Catalog
methods.description: Returns a bundle file of the listed tables and pipelines with their dependency closure, computed in both directions; an empty or absent list exports every exportable object. System tables travel by name, as required system tables; OTLP landing tables and PENDING/FAILED tables are left out. Each table needs TABLE_GET, and one with sensitive columns the caller may not see is refused (403 `sensitive_column_not_entitled`), and one with a column a column policy hides from the caller is refused 403 `column_not_entitled`, checked across every bundle table first. Access (privileges, row policies and column policies) travels only with `include_access: true`, which requires TABLE_GRANT and covers system tables too: only what a PUT would accept now is carried, and an enrichment a column policy names joins the export.

methods.name: getDashboard

methods.name: getEntitySchema
methods.title: Get Entity Schema

methods.name: getOtelSink

methods.name: getPipeline
methods.title: Get Pipeline
methods.description: Returns the declaration plus its read-only runtime state. Read with `view=compiled`, an `enrich` pipeline additionally carries the resolved `response_schema` the model is held to, its derived grain key, version column and output mapping, and its resolved read source; the ADAS-driven cursor and schedule members are absent for it on either projection, because its scan position is held by the Enrichment Runner. A `view=compiled` read of a declaration that cannot be compiled — one still missing a member its kind requires, or a complete one whose outputs compose to no response schema — is refused with 422 `pipeline_validation_failed` naming the problem.

parameters.name: view

methods.name: getPipelineRevision
methods.title: Get Pipeline Revision
methods.summary: Get a pipeline as it stood at a revision
methods.description: Returns the pipeline's own stored fields reconstructed from the audit trail at the end of the given revision. 404 if the pipeline did not exist at that revision or the revision is unknown. Revision ids come from the activity feed. Gated the same as the live read: any mapped application role.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision id, as carried by an activity

methods.title: Get Saved Query
methods.description: Returns the full object including its body, exactly as persisted. A saved query the caller may not see is reported as not found.

methods.name: getSavedQueryRevision
methods.title: Get Saved Query Revision
methods.summary: Get a saved query as it stood at a revision
methods.description: Returns the saved query's own stored fields reconstructed from the audit trail at the end of the given revision. 404 if the saved query did not exist at that revision, the revision is unknown, or the caller may not currently see it (visibility is resolved against the saved query's current scope/owner, not its historical one, so a personal saved query's history is readable by its owner alone and a deleted saved query's history by no one). Revision ids come from the activity feed.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision id, as carried by an activity

methods.name: getSessionsSource
methods.title: Get Sessions Source
methods.description: The stored setting as written, with the time and author of its last write.

methods.name: getTable
methods.title: Get Table
methods.description: Returns the definition and its exposed columns.

methods.name: getTableAccess
methods.title: Get Table Access
methods.summary: List a table's access entries, or read one role's entry
methods.description: Without `role`, returns `{generation, roles, ineffective_grants}`: every role's entry on the table, keyed and sorted by role, the table's access `generation`, and every entry's report grouped by role in that order; 403 without TABLE_GRANT, then 404 for an unknown table. With `role`, returns `{generation, role, privileges, rows, columns, ineffective_grants}`: that role's entry, the generation and that entry's report; 400 for a blank or repeated role, 403 without TABLE_GRANT, then 404 for an unknown table, then 404 when the role has no entry. `ineffective_grants` is the report a PUT returns, judged on the entries as stored at the read, and `[]` when empty.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Optional: omit it to list every role's entry, give it to read one role's. Raw provider role, sent as an ordinary URL-encoded query value (role `/analytics/viewers` is `?role=%2Fanalytics%2Fviewers`, `team%ops` is `?role=team%25ops`). Any character is allowed. Trimmed; blank, or given more than once, is 400 bad_request.

responses.description: Every entry without `role`, one role's entry with it

methods.name: getTableRevision
methods.title: Get Table Revision
methods.summary: Get a table definition as it stood at a revision
methods.description: Returns the same shape as GET /{name}, reconstructed from the audit trail at the end of the given revision — the columns, ordering key and grain it had then, excluding columns dropped by then. 404 if the table did not exist at that revision or the revision is unknown, and at every revision of a non-system table whose creation predates the audit trail. A system table answers at every revision from the first recorded state of its definition. It shows the definition last recorded at or before the revision (a migration's change shows from the table's next recorded change) and no `columns` member: the trail does not track its columns, so `permissions.columns_restricted` is true whenever a column policy confines the caller. Revision ids come from the activity feed. A caller holding TABLE_GRANT (every caller in `none` mode) additionally receives the table's access entries as `roles`, as of that revision. A column is hidden when that revision's column policies or the current ones of the table's life containing it hide it from the caller: the live table's while that life runs, otherwise those it had when it was deleted, so a table created again under the same name never judges an earlier one's revisions. An enrichment's columns are judged by its source's: the source's own life while the enrichment's runs, otherwise the source as it stood just before the enrichment was deleted. Every column is hidden when no state of the table or of its source is recorded.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision id, as carried by an activity

methods.name: importCatalog
methods.title: Import Catalog
methods.description: Runs the same validation pass as the preview and, only if it finds no problem, creates each object in dependency order as its own step: tables, then pipelines, always disabled, and, with `include_access=true`, the bundle's access entries last, in one transaction; without it no access is written. On a failure part-way it deletes again what it created. 409 catalog_import_conflict under FAIL_IF_EXISTS when an object exists; 422 catalog_import_invalid when the pass finds a problem — the preview reports each one.

parameters.name: resolution_policy
parameters.description: What to do with a bundle object that already exists: FAIL_IF_EXISTS refuses the import (409), SKIP_IF_EXISTS keeps the existing object unchanged and imports the rest. OVERWRITE is refused (422): import never changes an existing object's definition, columns or pipeline. An existing access entry never conflicts: with include_access, the bundle's entries are written under either policy.

parameters.name: acknowledge_reused_names
parameters.description: Accept creating a pipeline whose name this environment used before. The Enrichment Runner keeps a deleted pipeline's scan cursor, dead letters and spend counters by name, so a recreated one resumes from them

parameters.name: include_access
parameters.description: Also write the bundle's access entries, per role, onto created, existing and system tables alike, never removing one; requires TABLE_GRANT. Default false: the bundle's access member is ignored.

A runtime cache, not a history: at most the 5 most recently started runs, cleared on restart and redeploy, and per instance, so during a rolling-update overlap it can omit a run the other instance holds. `state=running` yields at most one entry. Not paginated.

methods.title: List Entities
methods.description: Lists the entities available as the `entity` value of a structured query (the catalog's materialized source tables).

methods.name: listOtelSinks
methods.title: List Otel Sinks
methods.description: Returns all sinks, ordered by name.

methods.name: listPipelines
methods.title: List Pipelines
methods.description: Returns registered pipelines, optionally narrowed by target, kind, enabled, and a lower bound on updated_at — every filter optional, all applied together. With no enabled filter this is the whole registry, disabled pipelines included: a listing reports what is registered, not only what is running — including drafts, disabled pipelines whose declaration is still incomplete and which run nothing until armed. Completeness is computed, not stored, so there is no filter for it; `enabled=false` is the closest proxy. A `view=compiled` listing omits an entry whose declaration cannot be compiled rather than serving it with empty members. `kind=enrich&view=compiled` is what the Enrichment Runner's sync passes — it runs only entries with `enabled: true` and holds a stopped one's work — and an `enrich` entry then carries five derived members beside the authored declaration: the resolved `response_schema` the model is held to, the derived grain key, version column and output mapping, and the resolved read source; without `view=compiled` the same listing is the authored declaration and costs no resolution. Ordered `updated_at` then `name`, so the order is stable across calls over an unchanged registry.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Narrow to enabled (true) or disabled (false); omit for all

parameters.description: Which projection to return: `source` (default) - the authored declaration - or `compiled`, the resolved executable form the Enrichment Runner reads. `compiled` requires `kind=enrich` and is refused with 400 without it, rather than answering with unresolved entries under the compiled name.

methods.name: listQueryFunctions
methods.title: List Query Functions
methods.description: Lists the closed catalog of functions accepted in structured query `fn` expressions, with signatures, return types, distinct support, and argument constraints. These are the DSL's `fn` names: writing SQL, use `GET /v1/queries/sql-functions`, since some names here are not callable in SQL and some signatures are written differently there.

methods.name: listSavedQueries
methods.title: List Saved Queries
methods.description: Each entry is the same full object the single read returns, body included. Defaults to the caller's personal saved queries, most recently updated first.

methods.name: listSqlFunctions
methods.title: List Sql Functions
methods.description: Lists every function-like spelling the ad-hoc SQL surface accepts (execute-sql, validate-sql, translate-sql, Flight SQL) — functions, operators such as `+` and `||`, and constructs such as `CASE` — each with its SQL signature, aliases, the DSL function it lowers onto, and a runnable example statement. The predicate and statement grammar (comparisons, `IN`, joins, set operations) is not listed.

methods.name: listTables
methods.title: List Tables
methods.description: Returns all table definitions, ordered by name.

methods.name: patchPipeline
methods.title: Patch Pipeline
methods.description: Enables or disables it, and/or re-declares it. A declaration change replaces the stored declaration (an omitted member is cleared; an omitted `target` is kept). One that leaves the pipeline enabled must supply the whole declaration and is validated in full; one that leaves it disabled is a draft save and is stored as given. Enabling runs the declaration gate over the stored declaration. Whether a declaration change is allowed while the pipeline is enabled depends on the kind: refused with 409 for `aggregate`, whose target would then hold rows computed two different ways; permitted for `enrich`, whose target is a grain-keyed replace-by-grain table where that is already how it behaves.

responses.description: The calling identity may not read a column the declaration reads: one a column policy hides from it (`column_not_entitled`, checked first), or a `sensitive` one it lacks the clearance for (`sensitive_column_not_entitled`); or it lacks the endpoint's privilege or the pipeline's grant

methods.name: patchTableSchema
methods.title: Patch Table Schema
methods.description: Applies add/drop/rename column operations and the optional ttl merge-patch (set/replace with a full object, remove with {}) as ONE multi-command ClickHouse ALTER statement — validated by ClickHouse as a whole, so it is rejected or applied in its entirety — plus catalog-only column metadata updates, on an ACTIVE table. Rejected (409) before materialization — define and materialize the schema first via POST /{name}/schema. Type changes and drops/renames of system, grain, or ordering-key columns are rejected (422), as is a drop of the TTL-referenced column. On an enrichment, dropping or renaming a column another pipeline reads, or one that receives a transform output of the pipeline targeting it, is rejected (409) naming those pipelines — checked before any ALTER is issued, so a refused patch leaves ClickHouse untouched. For an enrichment, this is where you add a provenance column an already-materialized target is missing — `pipeline_generation` (long), `model` (string), `enriched_at` (timestamp), `group_version` (long), `truncated` (boolean); one that is absent is silently skipped on write. This endpoint does **not** inject them: it applies exactly the operations you list, because widening an explicit operation list into a five-column DDL on a populated table is not something to do on a caller's behalf. `pipeline_generation` is the exception you do not have to add by hand: a startup reconciler adds it to every enrichment an `enrich` pipeline targets. On an `llm` target, a patch that edits a column's `description` bumps the targeting pipeline's `generation`, because an output's prose defaults to that description and it is therefore a live input to the composed prompt. A column a column policy hides from the caller is unknown to it (422), and while the stored TTL is on such a column any `ttl` member is refused 403 `column_not_entitled`. A rename rewrites the column policies naming the column and a drop prunes them (each bumping the access generation of the table whose lists change, the source's for an enrichment column); a drop that would empty a list is refused 409 `column_in_column_policy` before any ALTER, after the row-policy guard (409 `column_in_row_policy`). 409 `table_busy` when another change to the table holds it past the lock timeout (retry).

methods.name: previewCatalogExport
methods.title: Preview Catalog Export
methods.description: Takes the export body and returns the objects the bundle would carry, each with the reason it is included, plus the system tables it would require and the objects left out. With `include_access: true`, `access` lists each table's roles and what stays behind (`left_behind`).

methods.name: previewCatalogImport
methods.title: Preview Catalog Import
methods.description: Runs the import's validation pass — the real create services inside a rolled-back transaction, then the arm-time pipeline checks — and returns what an import would do with each object, and with `include_access=true` with each access entry under `access`. Answers 200 whenever the bundle parses, problems included.

parameters.name: resolution_policy
parameters.description: What to do with a bundle object that already exists: FAIL_IF_EXISTS refuses the import (409), SKIP_IF_EXISTS keeps the existing object unchanged and imports the rest. OVERWRITE is refused (422): import never changes an existing object's definition, columns or pipeline. An existing access entry never conflicts: with include_access, the bundle's entries are written under either policy.

parameters.name: acknowledge_reused_names
parameters.description: Accept creating a pipeline whose name this environment used before. The Enrichment Runner keeps a deleted pipeline's scan cursor, dead letters and spend counters by name, so a recreated one resumes from them

parameters.name: include_access
parameters.description: Also write the bundle's access entries, per role, onto created, existing and system tables alike, never removing one; requires TABLE_GRANT. Default false: the bundle's access member is ignored.

methods.name: previewPipeline
methods.title: Preview Pipeline
methods.description:
Writes nothing, calls no model, and is allowed on a disabled pipeline — this is the checkpoint between declaring a pipeline and letting it write. A disabled pipeline is refused exactly as arming it would be refused; an enabled `aggregate` is re-gated too, an enabled `enrich` is not.

**Both kinds answer in one shape**, carrying only what a preview alone can know: `rows` (newest first; a group's members in assembly order), typed `columns`, the declaration as a portable `statement` (ADAS SQL) and `query` (structured-query DSL) a caller can run through the query API where there is one, `total_rows` (aggregate only: the number of rows the target holds once caught up), `group_key` (group pipelines) and coded `notes`. Nothing the pipeline read serves is echoed — read `GET /v1/pipelines/{name}` (and `?view=compiled` for an enrich pipeline) for the declaration beside it.

For an `aggregate` pipeline the sample covers the ENTIRE input, deliberately unwindowed, and takes no body. For an `enrich` pipeline the sample is read through the governed scan, group-assembly or materialize path, so it shows only what the pipeline itself may read; no prompt is rendered, because the renderer lives in the Enrichment Runner. The optional body narrows the sample — `from`/`to` for a row-grain or Class-1 pipeline, `group_key` for a group one (without it, the newest group is sampled). Every value is capped at 2048 bytes in `rows`.

responses.description: The sample, its typed columns and coded notes
A malformed body, or one carrying an unknown member such as `cursor` (`bad_request`)

The caller may not read a column the declaration reads — one a column policy hides from it (`column_not_entitled`, checked first) or a `sensitive` one it lacks the clearance for (`sensitive_column_not_entitled`) —, is row-confined (`row_policy_confined`), lacks the target's grant (`pipeline_access_denied`), or lacks `REGISTRY_ADMIN` (`forbidden`)
A conflict arming would also report (`pipeline_conflict`, `table_is_system`)

Requires the pipeline to be enabled (409 otherwise): a disabled pipeline never writes, which is what makes the preview gate meaningful.

methods.name: replaceTableAccess
methods.title: Replace Table Access
methods.description: Replaces the role's whole entry: absent or null `privileges` means none, absent `rows` or `columns` means null, and no other role's entry changes. An entry left with no privileges, no `rows` and no `columns` is removed. `generation` is the table's generation as last read: a PUT that would store exactly the entry the role already has answers 200 and writes nothing, whatever generation it carries (a retry is safe); otherwise a generation above the table's, or older than the role's last change, is refused 409 access_conflict (read the access again and reapply), while a change to another role since the read does not conflict. A missing or non-integer generation is 422. A PUT that changes the entry increments the generation by one. `rows` is `{"filter": ...}` or `{"where": "<SQL condition>"}`, stored and returned as `filter`. `columns` is a non-empty allowlist of the table's exposed column names and `<enrichment>.<column>` for its enrichments' columns. Checks run in this order: 400 for a missing, blank or repeated role or a body that does not bind, 403, 404 unknown table, 409 enrichment_follows_source (an enrichment's entry takes only write and modify, judged on the body as sent), 422 unusable generation, 200 unchanged entry, 409 access_conflict, 422 role (bundle or privilege name), 409 table_is_system (write or modify on a system table), then the remaining 422 checks. 409 table_busy when another change to the table holds it past the lock timeout. `ineffective_grants` reports privileges that change nothing: already_global, sensitive_without_verb, lifts_row_policies and lifts_column_policies; and the standing warning everyone_reads_all_rows, a read for `*` with no row policy on a table that is not an enrichment.

methods.name: translateQuery

methods.summary: Translate a structured query to SQL
methods.description: Validates the structured query with the same rules as `/v1/queries/execute` (entity and field validation, closed function catalog, offset paging with maximum limit 1000) and, without executing it, renders it as a single SELECT statement in the SQL subset accepted by `/v1/queries/execute-sql`. Contains operators render exactly: `co`/`nc` → `LIKE`/`NOT LIKE` (case-sensitive), `ico`/`inc` → `ILIKE`/`NOT ILIKE` (case-insensitive). DSL constructs the SQL subset cannot express — a contains value containing `%` or `_`, a null literal outside `eq`/`ne`, `include_total`, `having` on a row-mode query, `distinct` on an aggregate-mode query, or an empty `select` on an entity whose source columns include an object/array-typed field — are rejected with HTTP 400. Contains matching maps 1:1: `LIKE '%text%'` → `co`/`nc` (case-sensitive) and `ILIKE '%text%'` → `ico`/`inc` (case-insensitive). `CASE` and window functions translate to the DSL's `case` and `window` expressions. A statement that joins, reads a derived table or CTE, or carries a subquery executes over `/v1/queries/execute-sql` but has no structured-query document and is answered with 400 here. The returned `query` document is accepted verbatim by `/v1/queries/execute`. ClickHouse is never contacted.

methods.name: validateSql
methods.title: Validate Sql
methods.summary: Check whether an ad-hoc SQL SELECT would be accepted, without executing it
methods.description:
Runs every check `/v1/queries/execute-sql` runs except the ClickHouse round trip: the statement screen, parse, star expansion, entity and field validation, the closed function catalog, DSL or composite translation, and the row governance (default limit 100, maximum 1000). ClickHouse is never contacted, so this is safe to call repeatedly while composing a statement.

The response is always `200` for a well-formed request; `valid` reports the statement. `valid: true` does not promise execution succeeds, for two reasons. The query budget (`query.budget.*`) is enforced by ClickHouse as the statement runs, so a breach is only observable then. And this endpoint resolves the catalog at `TABLE_GET` while execute-sql resolves it at `TABLE_READ`, so a caller entitled to a table's schema but not its rows is answered `valid: true` here and `400 entity not queryable` there — deliberately, since composing a statement discloses schema rather than data, but it means `valid` answers whether the shape would be accepted, not whether this caller may run it. `warnings` carries advisory notes for the shapes that pass every check and still tend to breach it, and for the default limit being applied; warnings never affect `valid`, and they are heuristics — a composite statement receives only the limit note, because its blocks reference relation columns rather than one entity's fields.

`issues[0]` is the rejection execute-sql itself would return, classified with a stable `code` and, where one applies, a `remedy`. Further entries are additional unresolvable identifiers, so a statement misspelling several names need not be fixed one round trip at a time; an unrecognised diagnosis is reported as `invalid_sql` with its message intact rather than guessed at.

Column visibility is the caller's own: a `sensitive` column is absent from a non-entitled caller's catalog model, so naming one is reported as an unresolvable column — the same answer execution gives, and deliberately so.

responses.description: The verdict — for a valid statement and an invalid one alike
Malformed request: a missing, null or blank `sql`, or an unreadable JSON body. An invalid *statement* is a 200 with `valid: false`.

Composes with `where`: the predicate chooses the rows, this deduplicates the values on them. Use it to count the entities in a group whose grain is coarser than the input's row grain — a `where` cannot express that, because which row represents a distinct value is a property of the group, not of the row. A distinct result is exact at the grain it is stored at but must not be summed across stored rows.

A measure carrying a `where` can yield NULL for a group in which nothing matches, so its target column must be nullable.

SqlTranslationResponseDto.description: The structured query DSL translation of a SQL statement.

query.description: The DSL document, accepted verbatim by POST /v1/queries/execute.

SqlValidationResponseDto.description: Whether execute-sql would accept the statement, and what it would cost

effective_limit.description: The outermost row ceiling execution would apply — the statement's own LIMIT, or the default where it carries none. Absent for an invalid statement and for a catalog-metadata statement, which no row limit governs.

issues.description: Why the statement would be rejected; empty when it is valid. The first entry is the rejection execute-sql itself would return; any further entries are additional unresolvable identifiers found so they need not be discovered one round trip at a time.

valid.description: True when POST /v1/queries/execute-sql would accept the statement

warnings.description: Advisory notes about a valid statement — shapes that pass every check and can still be refused at execution by the query budget. Heuristics, never verdicts.

clamp.description: What held the last run's window short of its input's available cursor, or absent when nothing did. A pipeline reading an enrichment is only as fresh as that enrichment: the window stops where the enrichment's values have actually been written, because reading a row whose enrichment cell is still empty writes a wrong result that no later run revisits. Read it as **progress**, not as an error — but a clamp that persists for more than a few enrichment cadences means the enrichment has stopped advancing (its pipeline disabled, or its runner away), and that does need attention.

cursor_identity.description: Tiebreaker half of the scan position

cursor_version.description: Scan position in the input's total order (epoch millis); absent until the first successful run, and always absent for a kind whose cursor the runner owns

drained_at.description: When ADAS last probed this pipeline and found nothing left matching its filter — a distinct fact from the position, and the one that keeps the position usable: the probe applies the filter, so non-matching rows sit above the position and are permanently unenriched by construction.

has_more.description: Whether the last run left input behind (it filled its window limit). While true the pipeline is working through a backlog and is re-run on every scheduler tick rather than on its own cron. Read this alongside `lag_seconds`: lag alone cannot distinguish a caught-up pipeline from one that has settled at a large constant backlog. **Deliberately unaffected by `clamp`**: a clamped pipeline is held back on purpose and waits for its own cron rather than re-probing every tick against a position that has not moved.

lag_seconds.description: How far behind the input this pipeline is, in seconds, measured against the present at the moment you read it — so two reads of the same unchanged cursor differ by the time between them, and both are correct. Expect a **sawtooth, not a level**: the floor is roughly the configured safety lag plus the run's own duration plus the input's ingest lag, and the ceiling is one cron period above that. It is **not** time since the last run — it derives from the cursor, so it bundles time-since-run with how far behind the cursor already was. Read it alongside `last_run_at`, `last_error` and `has_more` to tell a stall from a healthy cadence, and set any alert threshold above one cron period or every cron slot will fire.

last_error.description: The last run failure; absent after a success

last_run_at.description: When the last ADAS-driven run ran (successfully or not)

materialized_through_identity.description: Tiebreaker half of the materialized position

materialized_through_version.description: How far ADAS has materialized this pipeline's target enrichment through, on the input's cursor axis — the end tuple of the last window it wrote. Class-1 `enrich` pipelines only (`transform.type: sql`), and absent until the first window is written. This is what every dependent rollup's freshness clamp reads.

next_run_at.description: When ADAS will next run this pipeline; absent when disabled, and absent for a kind ADAS drives no schedule for

rebuild_required.description: Set when an enrichment this pipeline reads had its history re-derived after this pipeline's output was last built, so values it already wrote may have changed underneath it. This is an **instruction**, not progress: no window is held back and no future run corrects it, because the affected input rows did not move. Rebuild with the operations the API already has — delete and re-register the pipeline, re-derive over the affected range with a windowed materialize, or recreate the target table first where a re-run moved rows between group keys.

unclamped_reads.description: Enrichments this pipeline reads that no clamp can protect, each with the reason. Empty for most pipelines. These columns are still read — the pipeline is simply exposed to the ordinary freshness gap for them, which is why it is reported rather than assumed away.

StructuredQueryResultDto.description: Rows produced by a structured query, plus an optional total row count.

rows.description: Projected rows as field-name → value maps, in field order.

totalCount.description: Total matching rows ignoring paging; only set for row-mode offset paging with include_total=true.

StructuredQueryTranslationResponseDto.description: The SQL translation of a structured query DSL document.

sql.description: A single SELECT statement in the SQL subset accepted by POST /v1/queries/execute-sql.
sql.example: SELECT "deployment", count(*) AS "n" FROM "dial_usage_log" GROUP BY "deployment" ORDER BY "n" DESC LIMIT 10

column_count.description: Number of exposed columns (list only; single-get carries `columns` instead)

columns.description: Exposed columns (single-get only; absent on a system table's revision snapshot, whose columns are not tracked)

identity_column.description: Physical column identifying one row of this source — the tiebreaker half of the tuple the governed incremental scan pages it by. Absent for an enrichment, and for a source that declares none, which is what makes such a table unscannable.

layout.description: An enrichment's current layout relative to its source (absent from the list and the revision read, and when there is nothing to report): `aligned` — partitioned like its source and joined on (grain key, partition column); `migrating` — ADAS is relaying the existing table out into that layout, by itself; `unsupported` — the relayout skipped it (an llm writer, a column it cannot adopt, or a database engine that cannot exchange tables).

partition_by.description: Time partitioning, if the table declares any. Settable only on a source; present on an enrichment when the catalog declares one, which claims that the column holds the same value as the source's partition column for the same grain key and lets a grain join prune the enrichment's partitions

permissions.description: The calling identity's effective permissions on this table. Read-only: computed server-side per request, never settable via the API.

roles.description: The table's access entries as of the revision, keyed by role, in the shape of the `roles` member of GET /v1/tables/{name}/access (no generation). Revision read only, and only for a caller holding TABLE_GRANT (always in `none` mode); absent means withheld, not empty.

source_table.description: Source table this enrichment enriches (enrichment only)

system.description: Whether the table is system-owned (managed by ADAS). Read-only: seeded server-side, never settable via the API. A system table is fully readable and queryable but rejects modification (update, schema change, delete, row write).

tag_order.description: Per-table ordering of column tag names (absent when not set). When set, the columns list is returned sorted by this ordering.

ttl.description: Row-expiry TTL (absent when the table has none). Declared via POST /v1/tables/{name}/schema and modified/removed via the ttl member of PATCH /v1/tables/{name}/schema.

version_column.description: Physical timestamp column carrying this source's row version — the column the governed incremental scan orders and safety-lags by. Absent for an enrichment, and for a definition that declares none.

write.description: Write discipline: `append` keeps every row (MergeTree), `upsert_by_key` collapses to the latest row per ordering_key (ReplacingMergeTree). Immutable — declared at create, since it selects the ClickHouse engine.

tables.description: All table definitions, ordered by name

Target.description: One subject named with its kind.

subject.description: The blob key or ISO date.

jsonata.description: JSONata over the model response (llm output vars only)

sql.description: Scalar expression over the source's declared columns (sql output vars only)

type.description: Logical type (string, long, double, boolean, datetime)

from.description: Exclusive lower bound on the input's version column (row-grain pipelines only)

group_key.description: The group to try, for a `group`-triggered pipeline; without it the newest group is chosen, as the preview chooses it

limit.description: How many of the newest sampled rows to return, 1 to 5; 1 when omitted. Refused on a `group` pipeline, whose trial input is the whole group

to.description: Inclusive upper bound on the input's version column (row-grain pipelines only)

input_rows.description: The rows the runner would receive, with no value cap: the newest `limit` sampled rows keyed as a scan row, or the whole group as `/group-rows` returns it

pipeline.description: The compiled projection of the declaration the sample was read through; for a disabled pipeline, as the gate derived it rather than as stored

preview.description: The response `POST /v1/pipelines/{name}/preview` gives for the same body, values capped

truncated.description: Whether the group fetch's row or byte cap cut the group (`group` pipelines only)

cron.description: Spring cron expression (6 fields, UTC); only valid with `schedule`. Required for an `aggregate` pipeline; an `enrich` pipeline that omits it runs every minute at a second derived from its name, and the resolved cron is stored and echoed

group_by.description: Group key; required for and only valid with `group`, and must equal the target enrichment's grain key

kind.description: `schedule` (row grain, cron-driven; the only kind an `aggregate` pipeline may use) or `group` (one firing per group key). `on_ingest` is retired and refused.

member_select.description: Member-selection policy; optional, and only valid with `group`. Omit to leave the group assembly's default policy (the newest members by the source's total order) in place.

ready_when.description: Readiness declaration; required for and only valid with `group`

column.description: Declared date/timestamp input column to bucket
Physical (source_name) column the TTL is computed over; a declared non-nullable date or timestamp column of the table

interval.description: Positive number of units after which a row expires; zero or negative is rejected (422)

description.description: New description; null leaves it unchanged

tag_order.description: Per-table tag ordering (merge-patch): omit/null to leave unchanged, empty array to clear, non-empty array to replace

write.description: Not accepted here (422): the write discipline selects the ClickHouse engine, which is frozen at materialization; it is declared at POST /v1/tables

column.description: A column of the read source's entity, under either spelling, or an enrichment column under its qualified flat name

jsonata.description: A JSONata expression over the scanned row, parsed (parse-only) at registration; runtime evaluation is the runner's

change_direction.description: Whether a rise in the figure is good news

description.description: Author-written description, shown to every viewer

id.description: Client-assigned id, unique within the dashboard

inline_query.description: A query this widget holds itself; exactly one of saved_query_id and inline_query

row_limit.description: Rows the widget fetches, from 1 to 1000

saved_query_id.description: A saved query this widget runs; exactly one of saved_query_id and inline_query
